questions.question: Explain map, filter, and reduce — and when chained versus separate passes.
questions.title: Array Methods Map Filter Reduce
questions.direct_answer: map transforms each element (1:1, new array); filter selects (predicate → subset, new array); reduce folds to a single value (accumulator + current → next accumulator). All are non-mutating and skip empty slots on sparse arrays. Chaining (arr.filter().map()) reads declaratively but makes multiple passes — for large data, one reduce (or a for loop) computing everything in a single pass is faster.

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The mutation boundary (the correctness line): map/filter/reduce never MUTATE the source array — but the callback can mutate element OBJECTS (map(u => { u.active = false; }) mutates every user). The pure pattern returns new objects: map(u => ({...u, active: false})). This is the same immutability discipline React state updates need — the array-methods idiom IS the React update idiom (map for updates, filter for deletes, spread for inserts).

The methods around the trio (the completeness layer): find/findIndex (first match, no intermediate array — the fix for filter()[0]); some/every (existential checks — stop at first verdict, unlike filter's full pass); flatMap (map then flatten — the monadic transform: words.map(split).flat()); sort — the trap: it MUTATES and sorts by string comparison by default ([10, 9, 1].sort() → [1, 10, 9]!). The safe form: [...arr].sort((a, b) => a - b) or the new toSorted (2023+, non-mutating).

The iterator-vs-array future (the senior framing): map/filter/reduce exist on Array but the SAME operations exist as generators — pipeline libraries build lazy chains where filter/map run ONE element through the whole pipeline before the next starts, and infinite sequences compose. The native move in this direction: array methods from iterators (Iterator.prototype.map in newer specs) + Object.groupBy/Map.groupBy (2024) — the reduce-grouping example above becoming a built-in. Knowing reduce CAN build every other array method is the classic proof-of-understanding follow-up: filter is reduce with a conditional push, map is reduce with a transform push.
